challenges.claim: Cyclic or self-referential cluster chain loops without termination
challenges.finding: CONFIRMED for a cycle whose cluster values remain in the FAT range: the only exits are an end-of-chain marker (FAT12 >=0xff8, FAT16 >=0xfff8, FAT32 >=0x0ffffff8) or FatGetFatEntry returning FALSE. FatGetFatSector's range check is ASSERT-only, but out-of-range sector reads can return NULL and terminate the loop with 0; the causal statement therefore needs the in-range qualifier.

challenges.claim: BytesPerSector is copied unvalidated and used as a divisor
challenges.finding: CONFIRMED at the pin: assignments at lines 320 and 335 (line 304 sets a constant for FATX) precede any validation; only TRACEs and a 64 KiB cluster-size sanity check appear earlier, and no zero or power-of-two check exists. Downstream divisors include lines 306, 328, 360 and the FatGetFatEntry sector calculations. Runtime consequence of a zero value NOT RUN.

challenges.claim: PR #9510 is an accepted or upstream-active fix
challenges.finding: NOT CONFIRMED: state=closed, merged=false, zero issue comments, zero reviews, zero review comments; unchanged since 2026-09-09T12:15:31Z. Current master fat.c is byte-identical to the pin, so no bounded traversal was merged there.

challenges.claim: PR #9510's proposed bound eliminates the hazard as written
challenges.finding: The patch does add a FatNumberOfClusters+1 bound and a SectorsPerCluster zero guard, but the check is ClusterCount > MaxClusters after increment, tolerating one extra iteration; FatReadClusterChain success-semantics changes are untested. Needs source review and regression tests before any promotion.

reconsider_when: executed crafted cyclic-chain and invalid-BytesPerSector tests in an approved disposable environment
canonical JIRA issue or upstream maintainer feedback on a fix
